title: arxiv_2505.03811v1
universal_lens: The structural unification of semi-supervised generative adversarial networks and positive-unlabeled learning is formalized via a dual-path discriminator. By introducing an alpha-weighted leeway term, the framework bridges categorical cross-entropy for known negatives and binary divergence for unknowns, creating a robust manifold for noisy label inference. Third-order statistics derived from time-series models capture longitudinal evolution; Prophet's hyperparameters encode temporal dynamics via trend, seasonality, and regressors.
gsi_mapping: Galaxy Sports Intelligence maps this dual-path discriminator to Bayesian conformal inference over athlete tracking data. The alpha parameter acts as a noise transition prior, allowing GSI to isolate true biomechanical anomalies from sensor noise or incomplete event tagging in high-dimensional telemetry streams. Bayesian inference on Prophet-derived hyperparameters enables probabilistic player behavior modeling under uncertainty, aligning with GSI's risk-sensitive decision frameworks.
gse_mapping: In Galaxy Sports Engine, the unsupervised path models latent tactical state transitions. The generator synthesizes underrepresented play outcomes (e.g., rare defensive breakdowns), while the supervised path enforces strict constraints on known formations, enabling precise simulation of dynamic game-state evolutions. Situational reasoning in GSE leverages state transitions between player engagement patterns, informed by third-order statistical features from Prophet-modulated time series.

primitives.name: ScarceGAN
primitives.verbatim_quote: Although related to PU learning problems, we contend that knowledge (or lack of it) on the negative class can be leveraged to learn the compliment of it (i.e., the positive class) better in a semi-supervised manner.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes weak prior knowledge of negative class distribution, assumes separability exists in high-dimensional feature space, assumes longitudinal data exhibits temporal dependencies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when negative class priors are completely absent or when positive class is not truly rare but merely underrepresented.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction via the discriminator's output as p-value for hypothesis testing. The generator's role becomes simulating nuisance parameters.
layer2.telemetry: Discriminator output variance across unlabeled set serves as uncertainty metric.

primitives.name: Leeway Term
primitives.verbatim_quote: It relaxes the supervised discriminator's constraint on exact differentiation between negative samples by introducing a 'leeway' term for samples with noisy prior.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes noise in negative class labels follows a known distribution, assumes discriminator can tolerate misclassification within the leeway.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when noise distribution is unknown or when leeway exceeds the natural margin between classes.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE sliding window state-transition logic where leeway acts as tolerance threshold for state transitions. Violation triggers corrective action.
layer2.telemetry: Transition frequency outside leeway indicates system drift.

primitives.name: Cost Modifications
primitives.verbatim_quote: We propose modifications to the cost objectives of discriminator, in supervised and unsupervised path as well as that of the generator.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes convex loss surfaces, assumes discriminator and generator losses are differentiable, assumes balanced gradient updates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when cost functions become non-convex or when gradients vanish/explode during training.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI risk-adjusted utility maximization where modified costs represent penalty for false positives/negatives. Generator cost becomes exploration bonus.
layer2.telemetry: Generator loss decreasing indicates effective exploration of rare events.

primitives.name: Semi-Supervised Bootstrapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: To this effect, ScarceGAN re-formulates semi-supervised GAN by accommodating weakly labelled multiclass negative samples and the available positive samples.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes unlabelled data follows the same distribution as labelled data, assumes sufficient unlabelled data exists, assumes initial model can be trained on small labelled set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when data shift occurs between labelled and unlabelled sets or when the initial model is too biased.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE recursive state estimation where positive samples are measurements and unlabeled data provides process dynamics. Negative samples are used for residual validation.
layer2.telemetry: Residual error on unlabeled data tracks system health.

primitives.name: Optimal Discriminator Odds Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: SOTA at the intersection of semi supervised GAN and PU Learning: (SOTA - State Of The Art) There has been some interesting work in using GAN for generating samples from an underrepresented class.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D^*(x): Optimal discriminator output (dimensionless probability). p_d: Probability density of labeled dataset (dimensionless). p_g: Probability density of generated dataset (dimensionless). x: Input sample vector.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes both p_d and p_g are well-defined probability density functions over the same feature space, and the discriminator has sufficient capacity to approximate the Bayes optimal classifier.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when support(p_g) is disjoint from support(p_d), causing the denominator to approach zero and the odds ratio to diverge to infinity.

primitives.name: Categorical Cross Entropy Loss
primitives.verbatim_quote: CGANs [41] and ACGANs [38] have been successful in medical image data augmentation applications, where a converged generator is used to output samples from an underrepresented class.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: CCE: Categorical Cross Entropy loss (nats or bits). N: Number of samples (dimensionless count). P_model: Predicted probability by the discriminator (dimensionless). y_i: True class index. C_{y_i}: Correct class set.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes mutually exclusive classes and that the model outputs a valid probability distribution summing to one across all classes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Suffers from numerical instability and infinite loss if P_model outputs exactly zero for the true class, necessitating logit clipping or label smoothing.

primitives.name: Leeway Weighting Parameter
primitives.verbatim_quote: Instead, we leverage this insufficient and noisy truth to our advantage via the leeway term.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L_S^D: Total supervised discriminator loss (dimensionless). L_S^{+D}: Loss component for positively labeled samples (dimensionless). L_{SD}^D: Leeway loss component for negatively labeled/noisy samples (dimensionless). \alpha: Mixing coefficient between 0 and 1 (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes negative labels contain a specific proportion of noise (estimated between 30%-40%) and that a convex combination of losses can regularize the decision boundary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If \alpha approaches 1, the model overfits to noisy negative labels; if \alpha approaches 0, the model ignores the supervisory signal entirely, collapsing into pure unsupervised learning.

primitives.name: Unknown Class Assignment Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: We do suffer from the problem of weak/noisy labels for the negative class, however our prior is very small and their densities are non-uniform.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: y_{true, U}: Assigned ground truth label for the unknown class (dimensionless indicator). \mathbb{1}_{\text{negative}}: Indicator function returning 1 if the sample belongs to the noisy negative pool, 0 otherwise.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes all unlabeled or weakly labeled negative samples can be safely aggregated into a single 'Unknown' bucket without losing critical discriminative features required for generation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the 'Unknown' class contains highly structured sub-manifolds that should be separated, leading to mode collapse within the generated anomalies.

primitives.name: ScarceGAN Dual Adversary
primitives.verbatim_quote: ScarceGAN: ScarceGAN is our proposed solution to solve scarce class identification problem.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D: Discriminator network (dimensionless probability output), G: Generator network (dimensionless latent space mapping), x: Input feature vector (domain-specific units), z: Latent noise vector (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: The data distribution contains a dominant negative class and a highly scarce positive class; the underlying manifold of the positive class can be approximated by a learned generative process.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the positive class exhibits extreme multimodality that cannot be captured by the generator's latent topology, or if the negative class entirely subsumes the positive support without any separable boundary.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's counterfactual simulation layer, where the generator synthesizes rare player injury states and the discriminator validates them against live biomechanical telemetry.

primitives.name: Vanilla Unlearning Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: Here, since positive samples are rare in the unlabelled set, the supervised classifier essentially unlearns the positive distribution.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L_sup: Supervised Cross-Entropy Loss (nats), P(y=1|x): Posterior probability of positive class (dimensionless), N_pos: Count of positive samples (integer).
primitives.assumptions: Standard supervised learning relies on representative sampling; gradient updates are dominated by the majority class when N_pos << N_neg.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Occurs precisely when the ratio of negative to positive samples exceeds the capacity of the loss function to maintain a non-zero gradient for the positive class.

layer2.mapping: Represents the baseline failure mode in GSI's standard Bayesian updater when priors are not heavily regularized, leading to complete collapse of belief in rare event occurrence.

primitives.name: AAE Verbosity Trap

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: MSE: Mean Squared Error (squared feature units), L: Log-Likelihood (nats), V: Verbosity rate / False Positive Rate (dimensionless proportion).
primitives.assumptions: Adversarial Autoencoders attempt to match the marginal distribution of the data; assumes distinct density peaks for positive and negative classes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under highly overlapping distributions where minimizing reconstruction error or maximizing likelihood inevitably triggers massive false positive rates (verbosity).

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's naive thresholding on continuous momentum metrics, where attempting to catch all micro-collisions results in an unusable flood of irrelevant alerts.

reasoning_traces.think: The mathematical derivation within pages 3 through 5 establishes a rigorous bridge between Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The core doctrinal shift is moving away from treating unlabeled data as purely negative, acknowledging instead that it contains a mixture of true negatives and hidden positives. The authors formalize the optimal discriminator D*(x) as the odds ratio pd / (pd + pg), which fundamentally measures the likelihood of a sample originating from the labeled dataset versus the generator. This theoretical foundation allows the introduction of a dual-path architecture. In the supervised path, standard Categorical Cross Entropy (CCE) is applied, but with a crucial modification for the negative class. Recognizing that negative labels are often noisy or weak, the authors introduce a leeway term governed by a hyperparameter alpha. By force-assigning an 'Unknown' label to negative samples in a fraction (1-alpha) of the computation, the loss function becomes robust to mislabeling. This prevents the discriminator from becoming overly confident on spurious correlations present in the noisy negative pool. The unsupervised path complements this by minimizing the Jensen-Shannon divergence, ensuring the generator learns the underlying manifold of the data rather than just memorizing the labeled subset. The synthesis of these paths creates a powerful primitive for handling extreme class imbalance, directly applicable to domains like sports intelligence where critical events (e.g., injuries, turnovers) are rare and poorly labeled.

(2014), but pivots significantly by integrating the statistical rigor of PU learning pioneered by Elkan and Noto (2008). It also borrows the stability mechanisms from Least Squares GANs (Mao et al., 2017) and the multi-class extensions of ACGANs (Oden et al., 2016). The specific handling of noisy labels echoes the noise transition models found in modern robust deep learning, effectively retroactively applying statistical learning theory to the unstable landscape of adversarial training.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, the generator acts as an opposing agent attempting to deceive the discriminator by synthesizing plausible 'missing' data points from the underrepresented class. The discriminator, conversely, plays the role of a skeptical referee, constantly evaluating whether a given observation belongs to the trusted labeled set or is a fabricated illusion. The 'leeway' term represents the discriminator's cognitive flexibility—acknowledging that its own training data (the negative labels) might be flawed, thus preventing it from forming rigid, incorrect priors about the nature of the opposing agent's strategies.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical anti-collinearity veto must be enforced between the supervised and unsupervised loss gradients. If the leeway parameter alpha is set too high, the supervised path will dominate, causing the model to simply memorize the noisy negative labels, completely negating the benefits of the generative unsupervised path. Conversely, if alpha is too low, the generator may collapse into producing trivial samples that easily fool the unsupervised discriminator but fail to capture the semantic structure of the positive class. Therefore, a dynamic monitoring of the gradient norms between LS_D and the unsupervised loss is required to ensure neither pathway dictates the optimization trajectory exclusively.

reasoning_traces.think: The mathematical derivation within pages 8 through 10 centers on the fundamental instability of standard discriminative boundaries when subjected to extreme class imbalance. We begin with the observation that a vanilla Semi-Supervised GAN (SSGAN), utilizing Cross-Categorical Entropy (CCE) for supervised components and Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) for unsupervised regularization, catastrophically fails to retain the geometry of the positive manifold. Because the unlabeled pool is overwhelmingly negative, the gradient descent trajectory systematically pushes the decision boundary to classify all inputs as negative, effectively 'unlearning' the scarce positive distribution. This phenomenon is quantified by the precipitous drop in precision and recall to 34% and 24%, respectively. Furthermore, alternative generative approaches like Adversarial Autoencoders (AAE) attempt to resolve this by matching marginal distributions via KL divergence minimization. However, due to the highly overlapping nature of the positive and negative feature spaces, optimizing for reconstruction error (MSE) or likelihood inevitably leads to a 'verbosity trap,' where the model flags a massive proportion of negative instances as positive to satisfy the density matching constraint. The introduction of ScarceGAN represents a topological shift. By decoupling the generation of the scarce class from the standard adversarial loop and introducing a specialized 'Bad Generator' and leeway mechanisms, it forces the discriminator to learn a hyperplane that is robust to the overwhelming negative prior. The resulting lift in precision from 14% to 48% and the stabilization of recall demonstrate that explicit architectural constraints are necessary to navigate the singularity of zero-exposure regimes in high-dimensional sports telemetry.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage back to the foundational works on Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) by Chawla et al. (2002), which first attempted to geometrically interpolate minority classes. It evolves through VAE-based over-sampling algorithms (Zhang et al., 2018) before culminating in the adversarial, distribution-matching paradigm of ScarceGAN, reflecting a historical shift from simple data augmentation to complex generative equilibrium enforcement.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, the vanilla SSGAN acts as an overly cautious agent that, fearing the penalty of false positives in a sea of negatives, completely ignores the existence of the rare event. Conversely, the AAE behaves like a panicked agent, screaming fire at every minor anomaly to ensure it doesn't miss the actual blaze. ScarceGAN embodies a sophisticated cognitive state: it understands the scarcity, actively simulates the rare event internally, and maintains a disciplined, calibrated response to the noisy environment.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict cross-layer veto must be applied if the 'verbosity' metric on the unblocked (negative) set exceeds a predefined conformal threshold, indicating that the generator has collapsed into simply mimicking the negative class. Additionally, if the retrocausal dependency between the 'Bad Generator' and the discriminator shows collinearity—meaning the discriminator is merely reversing the generator's specific noise injection rather than learning intrinsic feature separability—the primitive must be discarded to prevent leakage of synthetic artifacts into the GSE state machine.
